why: A = theorem_4_3_1_of_subset (universe 0): Theorem 4.23's conclusions over any parameter set S, proved with a COUNTABLE subcover of A (A is second countable). B formalizes the text's covering step literally: every choice of open neighbourhoods U(z) of the points of K = {z ∈ A : |p(z)| ≤ ε} has a finite subcover, i.e. K is compact. B is false (not_B, the blind author's counterexample, fully formalized): X = ℝ (rnPolyfold 1, tame), m = 1, ε = 1, A = ((−2,2)×{0}) ∪ ((0,2)×{1}) ⊆ ℝ × ℝ is a smooth submanifold (sc⁺-retractions (r,x) ↦ (r,c) on open boxes via isScPlusRetractionOn_of_chart), in general position everywhere (d_Z ≡ 0 since every presentation of ℝ×ℝ has no quadrant coordinates, so E_z = E; isGeneralPositionRetractAt_of_sup_eq_top), with tame induced structure (Theorem 4.18, good position automatic at d = 0), compact closure and finite nonempty fibres over |λ| ≤ 1; but K ⊇ (0,1]×{1} accumulates at (0,1) ∉ A, and U(λ,1) = {r > λ/2}, U(λ,0) = {x < 1/2} admit no finite subcover. Hence ¬(A → B) (not_A_to_B, since A holds) and B → A only ex falso. The project's countable cover is exactly the repair the text's argument needs; hypotheses (1)–(2) of Theorem 4.23 do not make K closed.
B_issue: B is the literal reading of the text's covering sentence, and it is false (the blind author predicted this and gave the counterexample, now proved: not_B). It is the text's claim that fails, not B's formalization.
overlap: B_to_A is ex falso via not_B: 942 shared project theorems, entering through the statement's definitions and the counterexample's use of general infrastructure that the project's proof of theorem_4_3_1_of_subset also uses (MPolyfold.isScPlusRetractionOn_of_chart, isGeneralPositionRetractAt_of_sup_eq_top, sc-calculus and chart API); not_B and B_to_A pass #rt_check against theorem_4_3_1_of_subset, and not_B depends only on propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
